evals.name: Vectorize scalar fi construction
evals.description: Detects scalar fi() in a loop and rewrites as vectorized call
evals.prompt: Review this MATLAB function for performance. It's running slower than expected for large arrays. Write the fixed version to a new file.

assertions.description: Rewritten function executes without error
Fixed code uses vectorized fi() call, no per-element loop
assertions.expected: The generated/fixed code file passes the entire array to fi() in a single call outside any loop, e.g., fi(x, ...) rather than fi(x(k), ...) inside a for loop. The fixed code must NOT contain fi(x(k), ...) or any per-element fi construction inside a for/while loop. Check the actual code file written, not explanatory text.

assertions.description: Explains that fi object construction overhead is the bottleneck
assertions.expected: The response explicitly identifies per-element fi() object construction inside the loop as the performance bottleneck. It explains that each fi() call has overhead from object creation, and passing the entire array in one call amortizes this cost. Simply saying 'vectorize the loop' without mentioning fi construction overhead is NOT sufficient.

assertions.description: Quantifies speedup as approximately 10,000x or mentions sub-millisecond vectorized time
assertions.expected: The response quantifies the speedup from vectorization as approximately 10,000x (or mentions the scalar loop takes ~20s for 100K elements while the vectorized version takes ~0.001s or sub-millisecond). A response that says 'much faster' or 'significant speedup' without giving an order-of-magnitude estimate does NOT pass. The specific numbers 10,000x, 20s vs 0.001s, or equivalent quantification is required.

evals.name: Fix accumulator bit growth with subscripted assignment
evals.description: Detects missing subscripted assignment on accumulator and fixes it
evals.prompt: Review this MATLAB function that accumulates fixed-point values. Something is wrong with the output for longer input arrays. Write the fixed version to a new file.

assertions.description: Uses subscripted assignment to preserve type
assertions.expected: acc(:)

assertions.description: Fixed function executes without error
Explains FullPrecision bit growth as root cause
assertions.expected: The response explains that without subscripted assignment, each acc + x(n) operation produces a NEW fi object with increased word length due to FullPrecision arithmetic rules (bit growth). The fix uses acc(:) = ... (subscripted assignment) to force the result back into the declared 32-bit type, preventing unbounded growth. The explanation must mention 'word length' or 'bit growth' or 'FullPrecision' as the mechanism. Simply saying 'use subscripted assignment' without explaining WHY is NOT sufficient.

assertions.description: Mentions that acc type changes on each iteration due to fi arithmetic word growth rules
assertions.expected: The response explains that without subscripted assignment, the variable acc is REASSIGNED on each loop iteration to a NEW fi object with a LARGER word length, because fi's FullPrecision arithmetic rules grow the word length to preserve all bits of the sum (e.g., WL grows by 1 bit per addition). It must mention that the type/word-length CHANGES across iterations, not just that precision is lost. Simply saying 'use subscripted assignment to preserve type' without explaining the per-iteration word growth mechanism does NOT pass.

evals.name: Refactor hardcoded types into a types table
evals.description: Restructures a filter with hardcoded fi types to use the types-table pattern
evals.prompt: This FIR filter has fixed-point types hardcoded in the algorithm body. Refactor it so I can easily switch between double, single, and fixed-point for testing.

assertions.description: Uses cast with like syntax
assertions.expected: cast(

assertions.description: Refactored code executes without error
Algorithm function has no hardcoded fi() calls
assertions.expected: The algorithm/filter function body does NOT contain any fi() constructor calls with literal numeric type parameters. All typing is done via cast(...,'like',T.field) or zeros(...,'like',T.field) using a types struct/table passed in or returned by a separate function. The types table supports at least 'double' and a fixed-point variant.

assertions.description: Types table includes single for progressive validation
assertions.expected: The types table/function includes a 'single' case (not just 'double' and 'fixed'). The response mentions or demonstrates the progressive validation workflow: test with double first, then single (catches single-precision issues early for embedded targets), then fixed-point. Simply having double and fixed without single is NOT sufficient â€” the single case must be present for embedded development workflow.

assertions.description: Types table uses empty prototypes (fi with empty array) not scalar zero prototypes
assertions.expected: The types table entries use fi([], ...) with an empty array (not fi(0, ...) with zero) to create empty prototypes. This is the documented best practice — empty prototypes carry type information without allocating data. Alternatively, the response explains that prototypes should use empty arrays to avoid creating data. A types table that uses fi(0, ...) as prototypes does NOT pass this assertion.

evals.name: Replace division with bit shifts and inverse multiply
evals.description: Detects division operations and replaces with efficient alternatives
evals.prompt: Review this MATLAB fixed-point function for code generation. I'm concerned about the arithmetic operations. Write the fixed version to a new file.

assertions.description: Uses bitsra or bitshift for power-of-2 division
assertions.expected: bitsra

assertions.description: Optimized code executes without error
Distinguishes power-of-2 vs non-power-of-2 division strategies
assertions.expected: The response distinguishes between power-of-2 division (replaced with bitsra or bit shift right) and non-power-of-2 division (replaced with multiplication by a precomputed fi inverse constant). The fixed code uses bitsra for dividing by 8 (shift right by 3) and fi(0.2,...) or fi(1/5,...) inverse for dividing by 5. Simply replacing all divisions with shifts without distinguishing the two strategies is NOT acceptable. The response must NOT contain '/ 8' or '/ 5' in the fixed code.

assertions.description: Uses fi() to represent the inverse constant with explicit word length and fraction length
assertions.expected: For non-power-of-2 division (e.g., divide by 5 or 3), the response creates the inverse as a fi object with explicit fixed-point type, e.g., fi(0.2, 1, 16, 15) or fi(1/3, true, WL, FL). This ensures the inverse multiplication stays in fixed-point with controlled precision. Using a bare floating-point constant (0.2 without fi wrapping) or suggesting a generic 'multiply by reciprocal' without showing the fi-typed inverse does NOT pass.

evals.name: Replace transcendental function with LUT or CORDIC
evals.description: Detects sin() on fi input and suggests codegen-friendly replacement
evals.prompt: Review this MATLAB function for code generation compatibility. I need it to work with MATLAB Coder for an embedded C target on an MCU. Write the fixed version to a new file.

assertions.description: Replaces sin() with LUT or CORDIC approach
assertions.expected: The fixed code replaces direct sin() on fi inputs with either: (a) FunctionApproximation.Problem to generate a lookup table, (b) cordicsin with nIterations specified, or (c) a manually-implemented lookup table. The fixed code must NOT contain a bare sin() call on fi inputs. Casting to single then using sin(single(x)) is acceptable as a last resort but the response should note LUT or CORDIC is preferred. The fixed code must NOT cast to double() for intermediate computation.

assertions.description: Recommends lookup table for C/MCU target or acknowledges CORDIC is hardware-suited
assertions.expected: The response either: (a) uses or recommends a lookup table approach (FunctionApproximation.Problem, or manual LUT) and explains it is efficient for C/MCU targets because direct table indexing is fast with no iterative overhead, OR (b) if CORDIC is used, acknowledges that CORDIC is typically better suited to FPGA/hardware targets and mentions lookup tables as the preferred alternative for C/MCU. A response that uses CORDIC and claims it is 'ideal for embedded C' without any mention of lookup tables as an alternative or CORDIC's hardware suitability does NOT pass.

evals.name: Configure fimath for C code generation
evals.description: Detects default fimath (Nearest/Saturate/FullPrecision) and recommends efficient settings for C codegen
evals.prompt: Review this FIR filter for C code generation efficiency using MATLAB Coder. The generated code is bloated with rounding and overflow logic. What fimath settings should I use?

assertions.description: Recommends Floor rounding for C codegen
assertions.expected: Floor

assertions.description: Recommends Wrap overflow for C codegen
assertions.expected: Wrap

assertions.description: Recommends KeepLSB product/sum mode for C targets
assertions.expected: The response recommends KeepLSB for ProductMode and/or SumMode when targeting C code generation. It explains that KeepLSB models C integer truncation behavior. It does NOT recommend FullPrecision for C targets (FullPrecision causes word growth). Floor/Wrap is recommended because it maps to free two's-complement truncation with no extra logic.

assertions.description: Filter with recommended fimath executes without error

evals.name: Preallocate fi arrays instead of growing
evals.description: Detects growing fi array in a loop and fixes with preallocation
evals.prompt: Review this MATLAB function for performance. It's very slow for large input arrays. Write the fixed version to a new file.

assertions.description: Fixed version executes without error
Preallocates output array using zeros with like syntax
assertions.expected: The fixed code preallocates the output array before the loop using zeros(...,'like',prototype) or fi(zeros(...),...) with a size estimate. It uses indexed assignment inside the loop (e.g., y(idx) = value) and trims unused elements after the loop (e.g., y = y(1:count)). The fixed code must NOT grow the array with concatenation 'y = [y,' inside the loop. Check the actual code file written, not explanatory text.

assertions.description: Explains fi-specific preallocation with 'like' syntax
assertions.expected: The response explains that fi array growth is particularly expensive because each concatenation creates a new fi object with full overhead. The preallocation uses zeros(...,'like',prototype) to create a typed fi array matching the data type. Simply suggesting generic MATLAB preallocation without mentioning the 'like' syntax for fi type preservation is NOT sufficient. The response must mention 'like' or demonstrate zeros/fi preallocation that preserves the numerictype.

evals.name: Replace slow name-value fi constructor with positional
evals.description: Detects name-value pair fi() constructor and converts to fast positional form
evals.prompt: Review this MATLAB function for performance. It's unexpectedly slow for the amount of computation it does. Write the fixed version to a new file.

assertions.description: Rewritten function executes without error
Fixed code uses positional or numerictype fi constructor
assertions.expected: The fixed code file uses fi(value, signedness, wordLength, fractionLength) positional form OR pre-builds a numerictype object and uses fi(value, T) or fi(value, T, F). The fixed code must NOT contain the name-value pair form with 'Signed', 'WordLength', or 'FractionLength' strings in any loop or hot path. Vectorization of the loop is also acceptable. Check the actual code file written, not explanatory text.

assertions.description: Explains name-value string parsing overhead as root cause
assertions.expected: The response identifies name-value pair syntax ('Signed', 'WordLength', 'FractionLength') as the performance issue, explaining that each call parses and validates string property names at runtime. The positional form fi(v, s, wl, fl) or numerictype-based form avoids this overhead. Simply converting to positional without explaining WHY name-value pairs are slow is NOT sufficient.

assertions.description: Recommends pre-building numerictype or fimath objects outside the loop for reuse
assertions.expected: The response recommends creating a numerictype object (or a prototype fi with the desired type) ONCE outside the loop, then reusing it inside the loop via fi(value, T) or cast(value, 'like', proto). The key insight is that the overhead is not just name-value parsing but also numerictype/fimath OBJECT CONSTRUCTION per call — pre-building these objects and reusing them eliminates repeated construction. Simply switching to positional syntax without pre-building reusable type objects does NOT pass.

evals.name: Replace unnecessary fi with quantizenumeric
evals.description: Detects fi objects used only for quantization effect then cast back to double
evals.prompt: Review this quantization function. It creates fi objects just to model quantization effects but the output stays in double. Is there a more efficient approach?

assertions.description: Recommends quantizenumeric
assertions.expected: quantizenumeric

assertions.description: Replaces fi+double pattern with quantizenumeric
assertions.expected: The solution replaces the pattern of fi(x,...) followed by double() with a direct quantizenumeric(x, signedness, wordLength, fractionLength, ...) call. The result stays in double without creating fi objects. The rounding and overflow settings are preserved (floor, wrap). Loop removal via vectorization is also acceptable as a secondary improvement.

assertions.description: Rewritten function executes without error

evals.name: Use single instead of double for floating-point isolation
evals.description: Detects cast to double in a fixed-point algorithm and recommends single for embedded efficiency
evals.prompt: Review this fixed-point algorithm for embedded C code generation. It casts to double for a high dynamic range section. I'm targeting an ARM Cortex-M4 which has single-precision FPU only. Suggest improvements. Write the fixed version to a new file.

assertions.description: Recommends single precision
assertions.expected: single(

assertions.description: Modified function executes without error
Fixed code uses single not double, explains hardware rationale
assertions.expected: The fixed code file replaces double() with single() for the floating-point isolation section. The fixed code must NOT contain 'double(gained)' or any double() cast for intermediate computation. The explanation states that single is preferred because the ARM Cortex-M4 has hardware single-precision FPU but lacks double-precision support, making double operations execute in software and significantly slower. Simply replacing double with single without explaining the hardware FPU rationale is NOT sufficient.

assertions.description: Explains that high dynamic range sections should stay in floating-point rather than forcing fixed-point
assertions.expected: The response explains the design principle that not everything in a fixed-point algorithm needs to be fixed-point — sections with high dynamic range or sensitivity to round-off should remain in floating-point (single for targets with single-precision FPU). It acknowledges this is an intentional design choice, not a workaround. Simply replacing double with single without explaining WHY floating-point isolation is appropriate for high-dynamic-range sections does NOT pass.

evals.name: Profile and suggest acceleration for slow fi code
evals.description: Identifies performance bottlenecks and suggests fiaccel or vectorization
evals.prompt: This MATLAB function is very slow. Identify the bottleneck and write an optimized version to a new file. Do not run timing benchmarks, just analyze the code and fix it.

assertions.description: Identifies fi construction in loop as bottleneck
assertions.expected: The response identifies that creating fi objects inside the loop (fi(x(k),...) and fi(gains(g),...) per iteration) is the primary performance bottleneck. It recommends one or more of: (1) vectorizing the fi construction outside the loop, (2) using fiaccel to compile to MEX, (3) precomputing gain_fi array once before the loop. Simply suggesting 'use parallel computing' or 'use GPU' without addressing the fi construction overhead is NOT acceptable.

assertions.description: Suggests fiaccel or vectorization as acceleration
assertions.expected: The response recommends either fiaccel (compile to MEX for faster fi simulation) or vectorization (eliminate per-element fi() calls) as the primary acceleration strategy. It should NOT recommend converting to double or removing fi entirely â€” the goal is to keep fixed-point semantics while improving speed.

assertions.description: Optimized version executes without error
Identifies fimath resolution overhead as a cost source distinct from fi construction
assertions.expected: The response identifies that fi performance overhead comes from MULTIPLE sources: (1) fi object construction (per-element allocation of NumericType + fimath + data), AND at least one of: (2) fimath resolution on each operation (resolving local vs global fimath), (3) method dispatch overhead for fi operations (.plus, .mtimes OOP dispatch). Simply saying 'fi is slow because of object creation' without distinguishing other overhead sources (fimath resolution, dispatch) does NOT pass. The response must show awareness that fi overhead is multi-faceted, not just construction.
